newsitem.title: KENYA: ATHLETICS-KENYA'S AGUTA UNCONSCIOUS BUT STABLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KENYA'S AGUTA UNCONSCIOUS BUT STABLE.

text.p: Boston marathon champion Lameck Aguta was still unconscious but stable at the private Nairobi Hospital after a car accident at the weekend, doctors said on Monday.
"It may be up to 48 hours before he fully regains consciousness," said one doctor, who declined to be named. "Before then, we can't forecast what turns there may be in his condition."
Kenyan Aguta, also the Commonwealth 10,000 metres champion, sustained head injuiries in the crash but a brain scan showed no serious damage. His hands and legs were fine, the doctor said.
Doctors said they were encouraged by his condition and had not been forced to consider life-support machines.

Police spokesman, Assistant Commissioner Peter Kimanthi, said Aguta was injured when his car lost control and landed in a dicth at Mau Summit, on the Nakuru-Kericho road in his native Rift Valley province.
Aguta's driver, who was driving at the time, and another man were slightly injured.
Kimanthi said police were investigating the incident.
